gaps.fact: Lombardy borders Switzerland, and Emilia-Romagna straddles northern and central Italy. Neither fact is in a chapter, a stem or an article; Emilia-Romagna has no region article at all.
Cool continental, the Court's category for both regions. Only the lombardy article describes the climate; no chapter fact and no stem name it.

Franciacorta may not be released until 25 months from the harvest (18 of them on the lees). The eighteen months are taught everywhere; the twenty-five month release floor appears nowhere in the Codex.

Secco, Amabile and Dolce, the three sweetness words on a Lambrusco label. The Régionale chapter gives the English meanings without the Italian words, the italy article lists them, and Amabile stands only as a distractor in i-z8h6d1xc and i-soo2ytq5; no stem keys any of the three.
Bellavista and Ca' del Bosco, the Court's two Franciacorta houses. Both are in the lombardy article's producers; no stem of either bank asks them.

Lambrusco poured by the glass loses its gentle effervescence quickly once the bottle is open, so the opened bottle has a short shelf life and the pour must be costed and stoppered with that in mind. Only a general Champagne stopper stem exists.

errors.where: js/regions/italy.json, lombardy, law.classification: "Franciacorta DOCG (1995) was the first Italian denomination reserved for bottle-fermented sparkling wine"
errors.claim: Franciacorta was the first Italian denomination of any rank reserved for traditional method sparkling wine.
errors.correction: Franciacorta (DOC 1967, for still and sparkling wine) became in 1995 the first DOCG reserved for bottle fermented sparkling wine. The first denomination reserved for metodo classico alone was Trento DOC, recognised in 1993, as the Codex's own Village stem c-fe52u3q3 keys; the Régionale chapter lombardy already says it rightly (the first of its kind raised to DOCG).
errors.source: Istituto Trento Doc, the Trento DOC of 1993 as the first Italian denomination for metodo classico; Consorzio per la tutela del Franciacorta, history (DOC 1967, DOCG 1995 for bottle fermented wine only); the Codex's own c-fe52u3q3.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 61 (Italy), Village 62 (Italy North), 123 in all; both categories are shared with the other Italian subjects, and by stem this subject's share is 4 Régionale (i-3pkikc35, i-ahjt0m4x, i-9upf5gj8, i-1vg1i5oq, with i-soo2ytq5 shared with Piedmont) and 10 Village (c-9vnolvf8, c-qrqhd1vn, c-wusonuuh, c-qixzscbh, c-7zyl7br8, c-v6si61cq, c-2vlwxgrz, c-8uvk5222, c-tq9bkub7, c-nc7pigon). Beyond the map: Sparkling Wine World holds three Lambrusco stems (c-9008dsd0, c-m6jffr6u, c-zjvrjwfx), Sparkling/Fortified/Sweet two (i-s218awga Franciacorta and Satèn, i-hjhhcm4m Lambrusco), Service & Hospitality the sparkling stopper. Lombardy is well served on Franciacorta's lees ladder, Satèn, Valtellina and Sforzato; Emilia-Romagna is the thin half, with no region article, no Village chapter fact of its own and no stem on its location, its sweetness words or the by the glass cell. Three Court cells to read with care in our own copy: the Court prints Lambrusco DOC with three subzones, while Lambrusco di Sorbara, Lambrusco Grasparossa di Castelvetro and Lambrusco Salamino di Santa Croce are each a DOC in their own right and no single Lambrusco DOC exists; it prints Franciacorta Satèn DOCG as if a denomination, while Satèn is a style within Franciacorta DOCG; and it lists Frizzante among Franciacorta's label terms, though Franciacorta is made only as spumante. One search spent, on the Franciacorta rules: the 2024 amendment (published in the EU Official Journal in 2024) changed how dosage sugar is counted and barred moving a wine between Satèn and Franciacorta after bottling, and left the Court's cells (Brut only, at most 5 atmospheres, Chardonnay with up to 50 per cent Pinot Bianco, 18 months on the lees) as printed, so no court update is logged.
